newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. Nasdaq wants share of Israeli privatisation.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Nasdaq wants share of Israeli privatisation.

text.p: Nasdaq president Al Berkeley said on Wednesday the U.S. computerised stock system wanted to play a part in Israel's privatisation programme by getting newly sold companies listed.

Berkeley told a press conference in Jerusalem that the Nasdaq International Markets Advisory Board had had a meeting with Finance Minister Dan Meridor earlier and had discussed Israel's privatisation drive.
"I don't think it is any secret that we ...want to get our share of those privatisations," Berkeley said.
Berkeley said that traditionally Nasdaq had not been thought of as a market for large companies, but that the high-tech companies that have listed with it have grown up and stayed.
Frank Zarb, chairman and CEO of the National Association of Securities Dealers, the parent company of Nasdaq, said Nasdaq had been "a capital raising engine to the Israeli economy."
He said Nasdaq was looking to shortly add an Israeli to the international advisory board membership.

Zarb said that Nasdaq continues to develop its fundamental market and that in the next several years it wanted to make a major drive to move outside the United States, increasing the number of foreign companies listed on the Nasdaq and attracting investors from outside the United States.
"We do have a strategic objective to materially increase the globalisation of the Nasdaq market," he said.

Berkeley said in dollar terms Nasdaq will shortly overtake the New York Stock Exchange to become the world's largest market in dollar terms. "We will shortly pass them (in dollar terms) if our relative growth rates continue."
Israel is the foreign country that has the second most companies listed on Nasdaq. There are 61 Israeli companies listed, 90 percent of them high-tech.
The average Israeli company on Nasdaq has a market capitalisation of more than 150 million dollars and on average assets of more than 100 million dollars and almost 100 million dollars in revenues.
In total Israeli companies on Nasdaq account for 5.5 billion dollars in revenue and 9.9 billion dollars in market capitalisation.
From 1990 to 1995 there were a total of 25 initial public offerings by Israeli companies on Nasdaq and in 1996 there were 18 initial public offerings.
